excerpt: We will make a significant effort to meet or exceed that performance standard. However, we will not necessarily delay AI development and deployment in this scenario.

excerpt: Earlier editions of our RSP defined "AI Safety Levels" with specific lists of required controls. We still use this concept to refer to, and distinguish between, present levels of risk mitigations—those that we maintain for existing AI models.
paraphrase: Earlier RSP editions defined AI Safety Levels via specific control lists; the concept is retained to describe current mitigation levels for existing models.

excerpt: (For example, our initial Risk Report uses this distinction.)
paraphrase: The initial Risk Report is cited as an example using this ASL distinction.

excerpt: However, when defining the risk mitigations needed for future levels of AI capability, we have found that providing a specific list of controls is overly rigid, and we instead prefer to focus on what sort of argument an AI developer should make (and what sorts of actors it should address) regarding the risk level from its systems.
paraphrase: For future capability levels, Anthropic prefers argument-based framing over rigid control lists, focusing on the case and relevant actors a developer should address.

The changelog entry marks the initial RSP version from September 2023.

excerpt: RSP-2024: This update introduces a more flexible and nuanced approach to assessing and managing AI risks while maintaining our commitment not to train or deploy models unless we have implemented adequate safeguards.
paraphrase: The 2024 update adopts a more flexible risk-management approach while preserving the core commitment on adequate safeguards.

excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
paraphrase: Key improvements include new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes inspired by safety cases, and new governance and external-input measures.

excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
paraphrase: The document notes that the most significant changes follow.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ASL definition changed
excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models).
paraphrase: The changelog notes ASL now denotes safeguard groups only, not models as before.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ASL definition changed
excerpt: We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards. This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
paraphrase: New Capability Threshold and Required Safeguard concepts allow safeguards to be applied more precisely to specific capabilities rather than broad categories.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The prior ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: Rather than triggering higher safety standards automatically, reaching this checkpoint will prompt additional evaluation of the model's capabilities and accelerate our preparation of stronger safeguards.
paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint prompts further evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation rather than automatically triggering higher standards.
